findings.reason: the mechanism as written adds a false landing row per settled run and contradicts its own "once each", so the node must be told to key the rule on the landing states themselves (`promoted`, `withdrawn`, `discarded`) rather than the pane word, and the done-when needs an arm proving the `complete → recorded` echo prints nothing.
findings.text: §14 says a `landed` row is "carried once each" and directs the node to extend `CARRIED_PANE_WORDS`, but `PANE_STATES["landed"]` is `{"promoted", "recorded", "lift-ended"}` (reckon/crew/ticker.py:322), and the producer really does emit `from_state: complete, to_state: recorded` rows — 8,575 lines in `~/.config/reckon/crew/watch/*.events` carry them, e.g. `r-20261012T203017434181-plan-review-of-jt60sa-power-supply-sources` at 2026-10-12T20:38:34Z with `next_action` "promote the completed review run once its verdict is read" — so a word-keyed rule prints a landing row for a run that has not landed, once per completed run; the narrowing of `_observer_exception` is what releases it, since today that echo is held back for a run whose delivery was shown (the code's own note at ticker.py:1096-1099 calls `complete -> recorded` "the usual one" among held-back rows).

findings.reason: as written the schedule is unbuildable in either order — §9's wiring node is scoped without `recovery_watch.py`, and §14 is dispatched before the node it declares it must follow.
findings.text: §14 ends "It runs after §4, before §5 and §7, and after §9's wiring node, which also writes `recovery_watch.py`", while §9's own write paths (:305) list only `reckon/crew/watch_unit.py`, `reckon/crew/runs.py` "if the lease side changes", and the new test, and §9's own comment (:371) says that second node runs "after §4 releases `recovery_watch.py` and `runs.py`"; the producer's start-up and lease renewal that `producer_start_decision` (reckon/crew/watch_unit.py:246) must be called from live in `recovery_watch.py` (it imports `producer_lease_seconds` and `watch_lease_renewed_at` at :39-41), so a node dispatched on §9's reasoning is fenced out of the file the call belongs in, and the open followup f-alwh-002 (:341-342) sends §14 next — a section that cannot run before that node lands.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_queued_failure_remedy` (reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:124), `_is_lane_hold` (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:502), `_retry_backoff_hold` (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:673), `stream_carries` (reckon/crew/ticker.py:1195), the comment above `CARRIED_PANE_WORDS` (reckon/crew/ticker.py:330-359), `RowPolicy._observer_exception` (reckon/crew/ticker.py:1514), `_is_own_start` (reckon/crew/ticker.py:1381) and `_watch_transition`'s own-run keying (reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:1916-1917) all resolve as cited; the extensionless hrefs in §1 resolve as `<path>.html` by the house convention.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §12's done-when now carries a base-revision negative control for both the `QueueFull` and the `ScopeConflict` arm, and §14's carries a producer arm for the reviewed run's id plus base-revision controls for the launch, the `in review` row, the landing and the dropped row.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both changed sections write code and a new test, and their negative controls are recorded in the node's own gate log rather than a scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — neither section carries a plan label, stage name or ticket number into a symbol, filename or comment, and §14 states the rule its comment must carry rather than a tracker reference.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §14's mechanism (extend `CARRIED_PANE_WORDS` with the pane word `landed`, plus narrowing `_observer_exception`) also carries the `complete → recorded` terminal echo, which `PANE_STATES` maps to the word `landed`, so every run that settles as `recorded` would print a false landing row on the real code path; the done-when's fixture has no `complete → recorded` arm to catch it.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §12 changes one reading of one queued-pointer failure set, and §14 carries one row set through one existing row policy, each with a single gate.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §14 requires §9's wiring node to run first and says it writes `recovery_watch.py`, but §9's declared write paths (docs/plans/a-live-worker-is-never-drawn-halted.html:305) omit that file and the open followup f-alwh-002 (:339-343) orders §14 next without naming that node.
